name: Finland
summary: Children are guaranteed half of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Finland has no trust law; foundations exist but family-benefit foundations get no tax exemption and their precise limits were not confirmed.
reserved_share: Direct descendants (and their descendants): half of what they would inherit on intestacy (Code of Inheritance 40/1965, legal share, claim within six months of notice of the will). The surviving spouse may keep the common home and household effects.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Finland is not a party to the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention (not in the HCCH table); a foreign trust needs case-by-case analysis. Foundations are governed by the Foundations Act 487/2015; Philea says private-purpose foundations may exist but only public-benefit ones are tax-exempt.
open_questions: Whether new foundations may be set up for family benefit under Act 487/2015 was not confirmed from the statute.
Tax treatment of foreign trusts held by Finnish residents was not sourced.
